scope: Phase 0 Part A of the single-file document spike, on macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Apple M1, system SQLite 3.51.0 (Apple build, THREADSAFE=2, ENABLE_LOCKING_STYLE=1) unless noted. Throwaway worktree, branch spike/single-file: crates/slop-engine (container prototype, CLI, tests/spike.rs, examples reads.rs, limits.rs, repro2.rs). Single runs unless counts are given.
question: Can one SQLite file hold the built app, the document and its attachments: packing, opening untrusted files, reads beside saves, blobs at the limits, failures, the writer lock outside the file, and crash recovery?

method.tests: cargo test --offline -p slop-engine --test spike (9 tests, all pass)
method.reads: cargo run --release --offline -p slop-engine --example reads: the production Store saves a 1,000-row checklist (Loro exports, DELETE journal, synchronous EXTRA, fullfsync) 200 times at a 150 ms cadence, every 50th save a checkpoint, with an assets table (400 KiB, 40 KiB, 120 KiB, 300 KiB, 2 MiB) in the same database read from a second connection every 2 ms
method.limits: cargo run --release --offline -p slop-engine --example limits: 10 MiB attachments; a 182 MiB document at every limit (2 x 25 MiB assets, 10 x 10 MiB attachments, a 30 MiB checkpoint, 100 x 20 KiB updates); a 64 MiB HFS+ disk image filled with 8 MiB attachments
method.race: STRESS=80 cargo run --release --offline -p slop-engine --example repro2 [--features bundled]: 80 runs of 20 production-store saves beside a reader thread on the same file
method.pack: Quick Checklist built with buildProject (packages/cli/src/build.ts), converted to a stage, packed twice with the engine

pack.quick_checklist: packs and verifies as a template; two packs give the same canonical hash (0fc00b5e70d051ed726a87dc11d55366, xxh3-128) and identical bytes; 228 KB file vs 204 KB directory package
pack.engine_binary: 3.2 MB release, 2.6 MB stripped (macOS arm64, platform SQLite). Linux not built here.

results.hostile_files: an extra table, index, view or trigger is refused by comparing sqlite_master with SCHEMA run in memory (SQLite's sqlite_autoindex_* indexes are expected); a 26 MiB asset is refused from length() alone in 0.6 ms; a template with updates, updates without a checkpoint, no app row, a ../ asset path and a foreign application_id are refused; newer storage, package format or runtime ABI give requires_update; CHECK(id=1) makes a second app row impossible
results.publish: create and duplicate publish with renamex_np(RENAME_EXCL): an existing destination is left untouched (Exists) and no temporary files remain; a rebuild replaces a template but never a document
results.registry: an flock on ~/.hitslop/live/<dev>-<ino>.lock (folder 0700) excludes a second descriptor in the same process and another process; SQLite writes beside it work; a rename while held gives Moved; a hard link gives Linked, before or after acquiring; a killed holder's discovery file is removed by the next holder
results.nofollow: SQLITE_OPEN_NOFOLLOW refuses a symlink anywhere in the path (macOS /var -> /private/var), so the folder must be canonicalized first, as today's store does

reads_beside_saves.verdict: passes: asset read p95 0.75 ms (bar 16 ms). A read that meets a fullfsync commit waits up to ~40 ms. Appends cost ~1.8 ms more at the median with a reader.

same_process_reader_race.finding: With Apple's SQLite 3.51.0, a READ_ONLY connection in the same process as a writer intermittently makes the writer's lock fail: SQLITE_IOERR_LOCK (extended 3850), errno 9 (EBADF). During a concurrent backup both the writer and the backup failed.
same_process_reader_race.mitigation: Open in-process readers READ_WRITE with PRAGMA query_only=ON (or read through the writer's own connection). Other processes (the CLI helper, a Quick Look extension) are unaffected.
same_process_reader_race.today: store::duplicate opens its source READ_ONLY in the app process while the owner can still save (Duplicate of an open document), so the race is latent in production today, in that window.
same_process_reader_race.fixed_today: store.rs: in-process readers (duplicate's source, Snapshot reads) open read-write with PRAGMA query_only=ON, falling back to read-only for a file this process can't write. Regression test readers_beside_an_open_document_never_fail_its_saves (300 saves beside a thread duplicating and snapshot-reading the open document) failed 3 of 3 runs before (31-70 failures, 'begin: disk I/O error') and passed 13 of 13 after.

limits.peak_rss_mib: 3 before, 44 after creating five 10 MiB buffers and inserting them; reads add nothing
limits.save_during_backup: a save from another connection waited 1,720 ms for a 1,721 ms backup of the 182 MiB file; the production store's busy timeout is 2 s
limits.disk_full: typed Full after 7 x 8 MiB on a 64 MiB volume; integrity ok, no journal left, reopens with all 7 attachments

crash.harmless_journal: an aborted transaction that had not spilled left a journal but an unchanged database; a copy without the journal was correct
crash.hot_journal: an aborted in-place rewrite of a 4 MiB attachment left a changed database (4.25 MB) and a 4.24 MB journal. A READ_ONLY open refuses ('attempt to write a readonly database'). A writer's open rolls back and removes the journal; the committed attachment is intact. A copy of the file without its journal passes integrity_check but holds the half-applied rewrite: the attachment no longer matches its hash.

findings: The container works: pack is reproducible, opening untrusted files is cheap (0.6 ms checks, 42 ms quick_check at 182 MiB), sizes are checked without reading values, publishing never overwrites, and a full disk fails typed and intact.
Run quick_check on every open: 42 ms at the largest allowed document.

Never keep a READ_ONLY connection to a document beside its writer in the app process: Apple's SQLite 3.51.0 fails the writer's locks (EBADF). Asset readers open READ_WRITE with query_only. Today's Duplicate already does this in a short window and should change regardless of the container.

Duplicate and Share of an open document should run on the owner's persistence queue with the owner's connection as the backup source: from another connection, a save waits for the whole backup (1.7 s at the limit, close to the 2 s busy timeout).
Asset reads beside saves are fast (p95 0.75 ms); ranges for media are cheap with incremental blob reads.

A raw copy of a crashed document without its journal can be internally consistent yet hold a partial write that integrity_check doesn't see; per-blob hashes catch it for attachments. Share must be an operation, and a crashed document must be opened once before it is copied.
A read-only open (catalog, Quick Look) refuses a file with a hot journal, so those readers fall back to generic artwork until a writer opens it.
NOFOLLOW refuses symlinked parent folders; canonicalize the folder first.

Part B: the real host opens, edits, attaches, closes, duplicates and reopens a single-file document; the page sees no difference (probe identical); opening 1,000 rows is as fast as the directory package (230 vs 226 ms median).

part_b.scope: Thin native slice in the spike worktree: hitslop-core container module (pack from a directory package, create, duplicate, asset reader, attachments, registry lock), Store::open accepting a single file, FFI exports, and SlopPackage, SchemeHandler, SlopDuplicator, SlopAttachments and DocumentOwner reading a single-file document. swift test --filter SingleFileSliceTests, real DocumentSession in an NSWindow.
part_b.open_edit_attach_close_duplicate_reopen: passes: title, an inserted row and a counter edit plus an attachment save into the one file; after close the folder holds only Doc.slop (no state folder, journal or lock file; the lock and discovery are in the registry); Duplicate and the original reopen with every edit and the attachment
part_b.policy_probe_from_database: identical to the file-served handler: workers (.js, .mjs), AudioWorklet and all three WebAssembly paths run, packaged audio plays and seeks through 206 ranges over database bytes, blob:/data: scripts refused
shortcuts_not_for_production: attachments use a short-lived connection on the owner's persistence queue rather than the store's own connection
attachment ids hash with the standard library in Rust instead of SHA-256
skinned single-file documents are refused; artwork, Quick Look, catalog and the CLI schema command were not wired
the registry honors HITSLOP_LIVE_DIR in every build
